standard.title: Develop and modify civic inquiry questions
standard.description: develop and modify questions to investigate Australia's political and legal systems, and contemporary civic issues
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can develop questions to investigate Australia's political and legal systems and contemporary civic issues (AC9HC8S01). At Year 9 the expectation adds modification — students are expected to revisit and refine questions as their investigation develops, not just formulate them at the outset.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop initial inquiry questions about Australia's political and legal systems or civic issues, and modify those questions as their investigation develops in response to new information.

nodes.label: Developing focused civic inquiry questions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop focused, investigable questions about Australia's political and legal systems or a contemporary civic issue.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least one question that is focused enough to investigate (not too broad, not a yes/no question) about a political, legal or civic topic.
nodes.typical_width: Develop focused inquiry questions about Australia's political and legal systems or civic issues; distinguish between questions that can be answered with facts and questions that require analysis and evaluation; practise constructing questions using the elaboration examples (e.g. 'How democratic is Australia's system of government?' or 'Does Australia's legal system deliver justice?').
wider: Develop question sets at different levels of abstraction (factual, analytical, evaluative) for the same civic topic and assess how each type drives different kinds of investigation
Practise developing inquiry questions from news events or policy changes, evaluating what makes a civic question worth investigating
Compare student-generated questions with those from published civic education inquiries and evaluate the differences in focus and scope
nodes.hinge_reason: A poorly scoped initial question prevents meaningful modification — students cannot improve a question that was never adequately formulated. If the initial question is too vague or simply factual, the modification work in Node 2 has nothing to build on and the investigation cannot proceed purposefully.

response_modes.reason: Students need explicit practice distinguishing researchable analytical questions from vague or simply factual ones. Working through several examples — identifying what makes each stronger or weaker — builds the judgment needed before they formulate their own inquiry questions.

success_criteria: Develops at least one inquiry question that is focused on a political, legal or civic issue and requires analysis rather than a simple factual answer
Explains why the question is worth investigating

nodes.label: Modifying questions as investigation develops
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can revisit and modify their inquiry questions in response to new information gathered during investigation.
nodes.minimum_width: Modify at least one inquiry question based on information gathered during investigation, and explain what prompted the change.
nodes.typical_width: Revisit initial inquiry questions as investigation develops; modify questions to be more specific, more accurate, or more relevant based on what has been found; explain the reasoning for modifications (e.g. moving from 'How democratic is Australia's system of government?' to 'How representative is Australia's system of government?' as evidence about voting systems is encountered).
wider: Document a full inquiry question development trail — initial question, modification trigger, revised question, and effect on investigation — and evaluate how modification improved the inquiry
Practise modifying questions across two or three different civic topics to build flexibility and transfer
Evaluate the inquiry questions used in a published report or civic inquiry and propose how they could have been better framed

response_modes.reason: Modifying questions requires students to hold their original question in mind, identify the specific gap or imprecision the new information revealed, and articulate the revision clearly. Regular low-stakes practice — e.g. modifying questions at the end of each research session — builds this reflective habit.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Question modification is a metacognitive capability that transfers across all inquiry-based subjects. Advancing students who can document and justify their question development are building a genuinely transferable skill, making this a high-value width investment.
success_criteria: Modifies at least one inquiry question during an investigation
Explains what new information or understanding prompted the modification and how the revised question better serves the investigation
